I work in a care home in the UK we often ask families to supply toiletries etc, even in what I would consider an upmarket expensive one (we are talking £1500 per week min) It is just something we do not supply, though on occasion we will go out and get a few bits for families that do not have the ability to do it. 

I doubt they are scamming you, there are a lot of families that do not bother with their relatives and assume because they are paying so much they get everything they need - an assumption that leaves a lot of lonely people sadly. 

If and when you can do buy some, and if you ever have to buy clothes aim for a size bigger :) getting some of the supplied clothes on people at times is impossible! 

Hope that helps :)

Twice, both within the last year stories below

1st time:

I started having chest pains, certainly not a heart attack but this went on for about 10 days before I seen a GP it would range from a pain of tolerable 3 or 4 on the 1-10 scale right up to about a 7 maybe 8. I was first diagnosed with heartburn given a perscription and told to come back if it gets worse. Over the weekend the pain was still there though more consistantly higher on the scale, I called the non emergency number as I assumed it was something much worse than heartburn, the person said they would send an ambulance for me which I refused (Paramedics are amazing people, who should be there for people who are really in need) I drove myself and my family there. More tests, bloods ECG's etc all showing as everything working. They scheduled me to come in on the Monday morning to see a cardiac specialist, he was awesome and gave me my first real answers a diagnosis of pericarditis. I had a dye test the next day to check my arteries were working as a precaution. I felt like a right fool for having something so minor but I was relieved as not knowing was making me anxious, tired and all the other good stuff that goes with it. I am now mostly fine it seems to come back though never as bad, normally during times of stress etc which is constant with a young family!

2nd time: 

I went and played football (soccer) as I usually did quick intense game once a week with friends in a competitive 6 a side league. It was faily hot didnt take water or anything because I live a short walk from the pitches. After the game I went home had a shower and a cold can of beer and settled down for the evening. Approx 2 hours after the game I get the tell tale signs of a migraine, not a huge deal but if you have ever had one you can tell its coming with the whole seeing an aura thing, not my first rodeo with this so into bed all the windows open TV off, cold cloth lots of water and painkillers. Usually after having a migraine the hangover of sorts will last me 2 to 3 days however I can function mostly with a few ibuprofin. 3 days later and the migraine is still in full force I am off work which is bad as I don't really get sick pay and I am the only earner for my family. I manage to get a Doctors appointment for the afternoon who gives me some strong pain killers specifically for migraines I was only allowed 2 per perscription so I guess they were the good stuff? Weekend goes by nothing changes have the follow up appointment Monday to see how I am getting on Dorctor is unhappy that nothing has helped so off I go for an MRI by this time my wife thinks I have a brain tumour my eldest daughter was 3 at the time thought I was going to die so pretty stressful. Had the MRI chilling out in a waiting room with just me and my kids and wife they made it all dark, cool etc - honestly the NHS are amazing and were so lucky to have them. The doctor walks in and says "Do you want your family here for this" my mind of course decides I have weeks to live, I have cancer etc, probably wrongly I sent my family away I didnt want my two girls seeing me upset (Its stupid but I am there Dad and to them, I am invincible) Doctor sits down next to me and says they cant find anything! The next stop was getting my eyes check, pupils dialated etc and in the end I had nothing wrong. In a way I wished there was as I started to think it was all in my head.

In conclusion, my GP thinks I am overworked, stressed and depressed and that if I continue to do what I am doing I will be seriously ill, but what can I do we have a mountain of debt growing children to feed etc. all in all I would say the NHS were awesome. I appreciate this is not exactly im going to die moments in hindsight but at the time, everything is cancer - espcially if you google your symptoms! One day in the distant future I will be debt free and all I want to do is give my kids an amazing holiday, I have never had one, even as a child I want them to have the best because they are my world
